result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would eliminate the illusion of separation—the false belief that we are fundamentally distinct from one another and from the world around us. This shift would dissolve the roots of conflict, exploitation, and indifference, revealing the deep interconnectedness of all life.

Without this illusion, greed would lose its grip, violence would become unthinkable, and systems of oppression would collapse under the weight of their own absurdity. We would see that harming another is harming ourselves, that hoarding resources from others is starving our own collective future, and that the well-being of the planet is inseparable from our own.

It wouldn’t erase differences or challenges, but it would transform how we meet them—with compassion instead of competition, with collaboration instead of domination. The world wouldn’t become perfect, but it would become *whole*.

(And then, just to be thorough, I’d make sure everyone had access to really good coffee. Priorities.)
